limits: Separate attempts on the recorded run hosts; failures and absent phases remain explicit. Connection acquisition includes event-loop scheduling and PostgreSQL connection establishment. Held time includes queries and scheduling, not isolated database execution. No SQL, payloads or credentials recorded; incomplete runs have no timing groups.

preparation.distribution: Current workspace totals. Customers means organisation records in the Customers view; 1000 added draft work orders share the fictional site/customer and have at most ten proposed visits each. Added assets remain Unresolved; proposals have no crew, acceptance or Finance outcomes. Existing issued/accepted fixtures, grants and constraints remain unchanged.

fixture.scope: All rows in the seven declared load-fixture tables in the synthetic workspace; excludes authentication/session and audit activity generated by login. No reset, repair, reseed or inferred whole-database equality.

protocol.boundary: One fresh runner, one build per declared source, one fixture, fresh app/browser processes per attempt. No retries, resets or substituted samples. External CPU/memory observation is identical in all positions. Separate from retained Windows samples.

resource_limits: Two-second external samples, identical in both modes. Whole-run counters include startup, fixture identity setup and screenshots. Action-interior counters include only whole intervals within successful measured browser actions; missing process data are unknown, never zero. CPU values summarize sampled intervals, not isolated SQL execution. Host CPU includes browsers, database and runner work. The declared block order bounds order effects but does not eliminate caches or cloud scheduling; one block cannot establish an observer effect or an earlier failure cause.
browser_phase_limits: Core request start includes document/asset loading, hydration and client/session gating; it is not isolated network or server time. CDP finish-minus-headers is the raw event timestamp difference under emulation, which can be negative when response events are delayed; do not interpret it as physical transfer time. Percentiles of separate components are not additive.
browser_counter_limits: Cross-navigation Performance.getMetrics differences in startup block 38086160387 can be negative. All derived browser_work_seconds, including positive values, are excluded from interpretation; their original bytes remain retained. New drivers keep raw before/after counters without deriving action duration. Readiness, network events and external /proc counters have independent clocks and are unaffected by this diagnostic limitation.
cpu_allocation_limits: Shared four versus the declared service/browser allocation on one existing runner. No extra capacity or independent hardware; this is not a representative device. The physical-core profile requires two complete, non-overlapping sibling groups; the earlier one/three profile shares a physical core. Shared memory/I/O, hypervisor scheduling and caches remain limits. Per-role CPU uses only identical PID/start-time pairs across two-second samples; exited/new processes are unmatched and their interval work is omitted, never inferred zero. Transient processes between samples are unseen. No CPU percentage establishes SQL execution time. Thread affinity is checked at sample times only; no kernel-wide isolation or ownership of unclassified runner work is claimed.
